items.method: narrative survey of LLM-based autonomous agents
items.finding: Proposes a unified framework for constructing LLM-based autonomous agents and reviews applications and evaluation strategies. The abstract does not report memory-specific effects on task success.
items.limitations: Broad survey; memory is only one component and the abstract gives no quantitative memory findings.

items.method: system design and implementation description
items.finding: Describes an agent-based business process management system with autonomous problem-solving agents that negotiate and coordinate. It is unrelated to LLM agents or long-term memory.
items.limitations: Pre-LLM (2000), off-topic; no memory component or evaluation in the abstract.

items.method: narrative review of LLMs and agents in chemistry
items.finding: Reviews LLM capabilities in chemistry and LLM-based agents with tool use, noting challenges such as data quality and the need for standard benchmarks. Memory design and its effect on task success are not addressed in the abstract.
items.limitations: Domain-specific review; no memory focus and no stated review methodology.

items.method: narrative survey of LLM-based autonomous agents (preprint version)
items.finding: Proposes a unified framework for building LLM-based agents and surveys applications and evaluation strategies. The abstract does not report memory-specific effects on success rate.
items.limitations: Preprint version of the Frontiers of Computer Science survey (duplicate); broad scope with no quantitative memory findings.

items.method: empirical agent system evaluation in Minecraft
items.sample: over 200 Minecraft tasks
items.finding: JARVIS-1 uses a multimodal memory to support planning with pre-trained knowledge and game experiences, and completes over 200 different tasks in Minecraft. The abstract is truncated and does not give the memory ablation numbers.
items.limitations: Abstract truncated; single environment (Minecraft); embodied multimodal setting, not purely text-based LLM agents.

items.method: empirical evaluation on nuScenes benchmark
items.sample: nuScenes driving benchmark
items.finding: Agent-Driver combines a tool library, a cognitive memory of common sense and experiential knowledge, and an LLM reasoning engine, and reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art driving methods. The abstract does not isolate the contribution of memory.
items.limitations: Driving domain; memory contribution not isolated in the abstract; the task is not a typical multi-step LLM agent task.

items.method: empirical evaluation of a memory-based RL policy on visual navigation tasks
items.finding: Scene Memory Transformer stores observations in memory and uses attention over them, outperforming reactive and memory-based policies on visual navigation tasks. This supports the value of long-term memory for long-horizon tasks.
items.limitations: Not an LLM agent (2019 RL policy); navigation only; no quantitative figures in the abstract.

items.method: empirical agent system evaluation in Minecraft (preprint)
items.sample: over 200 Minecraft tasks
items.finding: JARVIS-1 uses a multimodal memory combining pre-trained knowledge and game experiences to plan, and completes over 200 tasks in Minecraft. The abstract is truncated and does not report memory ablation results.
items.limitations: Abstract truncated; preprint version of the TPAMI paper (duplicate); single environment; embodied multimodal setting.

items.method: empirical comparison of single-agent, multi-agent and stochastic baselines
items.sample: two chemical applications (CO adsorption on Cu adatoms and on M–N–C catalysts)
items.finding: Hierarchical multi-agent LLM reasoning reduced the required atomistic simulations by up to 90% relative to heuristic or random selection. The abstract does not discuss long-term memory.
items.limitations: Hierarchical reasoning is not memory architecture; chemistry-specific; memory not evaluated.

items.method: empirical evaluation of a graph-based memory agent against memory and RL baselines in text games
items.sample: interactive text game environments of varying complexity
items.finding: AriGraph builds and updates a memory graph that integrates semantic and episodic memory, and the Ariadne agent markedly outperforms other memory methods (full history, summarization, retrieval augmentation) and strong RL baselines on text-game tasks. It is also competitive with dedicated knowledge-graph methods.
items.limitations: Text-game environments only; abstract gives no numerical results; preprint.

items.method: empirical comparison of memory structures and retrieval methods across 4 tasks and 6 datasets
items.sample: four tasks, six datasets
items.finding: Different memory structures (chunks, triples, atomic facts, summaries, mixed) suit different tasks, and mixed memory is resilient in noisy settings. Iterative retrieval consistently outperforms single-step retrieval and reranking.
items.limitations: Tasks are mainly QA and dialogue rather than multi-step agent tasks; abstract is truncated.

items.method: framework proposal with experiments (details unclear from abstract)
items.finding: Describes LLM agents as computational graphs with automatic node (prompt) and edge (orchestration) optimizers. The abstract does not address long-term memory.
items.limitations: Graphs here are about agent orchestration, not memory; no quantitative results in abstract.

items.method: narrative review/theoretical discussion
items.finding: Argues that experimental amnesia in animals reflects, at least in part, retrieval deficits rather than storage failure. It is about biological memory, not LLM agents.
items.limitations: Neuroscience paper, off-topic for LLM agents.

items.method: method proposal with empirical evaluation (details unclear from abstract)
items.finding: RAP retrieves past experiences relevant to the current context to enhance planning, reporting SOTA in textual scenarios and improved multimodal agent performance on embodied tasks. This links experience memory retrieval to planning.
items.limitations: Abstract gives no numbers, benchmarks, or ablations.

items.method: empirical analysis plus method proposal (SeCom) evaluated on benchmarks
items.sample: LOCOMO and Long-MT-Bench+ benchmarks
items.finding: Memory unit granularity matters, and prompt compression (LLMLingua-2) works as a denoiser to improve retrieval accuracy. Segment-level memory (SeCom) significantly outperforms baselines on long-term conversation benchmarks.
items.limitations: Focuses on conversational QA, not multi-step task success.

items.method: method proposal (TRAD) with empirical evaluation (details unclear from abstract)
items.finding: Step-level thought retrieval and aligned decision select more helpful demonstrations with less irrelevant context than trajectory-level retrieval. It targets sequential decision tasks such as web navigation and online shopping.
items.limitations: Abstract truncated; results and benchmarks not stated; the retrieved demonstrations are in-context examples rather than a long-term memory store.

items.method: method proposal with jointly trained write/read operators (details unclear from abstract)
items.finding: Proposes memory-centric adaptation so that memory written by one LLM can be consumed by another, via profile-conditioned write and read operators. The abstract states no results.
items.limitations: Preprint; abstract truncated with no quantitative results.

items.method: method proposal with evaluation on three benchmarks
items.sample: three heterogeneous benchmarks (conversational QA, multi-hop retrieval, web agent tasks)
items.finding: PlugMem structures episodic memory into a knowledge-centric memory graph to reduce context explosion from raw retrieval. It is evaluated unchanged across three heterogeneous benchmarks.
items.limitations: Preprint; abstract gives no result numbers.

items.method: method proposal (MRAgent) with benchmark experiments
items.sample: LoCoMo and LongMemEval benchmarks
items.finding: A Cue-Tag-Content memory graph with active reconstruction improves over strong baselines by up to 23% while reducing token and runtime cost. Retrieval is adapted dynamically to the reasoning context.
items.limitations: Preprint; benchmarks are conversational long-memory QA rather than multi-step task execution.

items.method: framework proposal with experiments across environments
items.finding: AdMem combines semantic, episodic, and procedural memory in a bi-level short/long-term design with actor, memory, and critic agents. Reward-based merging and pruning are reported to improve robustness and success on long multi-turn tasks.
items.limitations: Preprint; abstract gives no numbers, environments, or ablations.

items.method: benchmark/environment construction with five evaluation tracks
items.sample: Five tracks: tau2-bench, MEMGYM-DR, SWE-Gym, MEMGYM-CODEQA, WebArena-Infinity
items.finding: MemGym is a benchmark for agentic memory spanning tool-use dialogue, deep-research search, coding and computer use. It reports memory-isolated scores that decouple memory from reasoning, retrieval and tool-use ability so memory strategies can be ranked.
items.limitations: Abstract is truncated and gives no results; preprint, not peer reviewed.

items.method: empirical evaluation on two-player zero-sum games with experience-memory agent framework
items.sample: Tic-tac-toe, Connect Four; multiple model tiers; MCTS opponents
items.finding: LLMs play suboptimally in simple games and lose to MCTS opponents, and obfuscating the surface form leaves performance largely unchanged. An experience memory with post-game reflection and rule extraction yields measurable improvements on tic-tac-toe without changing model weights.
items.limitations: Improvement shown only on tic-tac-toe in the abstract; simple game domain; preprint.

items.method: unclear from abstract (method proposal, LLM agent with memory and reasoning modules)
items.finding: Proposes AGR, an LLM agent for group recommendation with a hash-table memory module supporting insertion, updating, retrieval, forgetting and summarization, plus a multi-step reasoning module. The abstract gives no quantitative results.
items.limitations: Recommendation domain rather than multi-step task success; no results in the abstract; preprint.

items.method: method proposal with benchmark evaluation and ablations
items.sample: LoCoMo and LongMemEval benchmarks
items.finding: REALM organizes memory as a heterogeneous cognitive graph with adaptive graph-search retrieval and retrieval-driven reconsolidation. It reaches 75.97% accuracy on LoCoMo and 65.11% on LongMemEval, beating the strongest baselines by 7.17 and 1.31 points.
items.limitations: Evaluated on conversational memory QA benchmarks rather than multi-step task success; preprint; abstract truncated.

items.method: empirical evaluation of a framework with ablations across tasks
items.sample: Sequential decision-making, coding (HumanEval), and language reasoning tasks
items.finding: Reflexion agents store verbal self-reflections in an episodic memory buffer to improve later trials, with significant gains over baselines across tasks. It reaches 91% pass@1 on HumanEval versus 80% for GPT-4.
items.limitations: Memory is a short-horizon episodic buffer across trials; preprint abstract is truncated.

items.method: narrative review
items.finding: Reviews evidence that sleep spindle deficits in schizophrenia relate to impaired sleep-dependent memory consolidation and thalamocortical dysfunction. It concerns human neuroscience, not LLM agents.
items.limitations: Off-topic for LLM agents; narrative review.

items.method: human behavioral and fMRI study with polysomnography
items.sample: Human participants (n not stated in abstract)
items.finding: Sleep spindle density predicted a larger schema benefit to memory over 24 h and reduced decay of schema-related memories. It concerns human memory consolidation, not LLM agents.
items.limitations: Off-topic for LLM agents; human neuroscience.

items.method: computational neuroscience modeling
items.finding: Shows that synaptic scaling combined with plasticity can separate short- from long-term memory storage in a neural model. It is not about LLM agents.
items.limitations: Off-topic for LLM agents; theoretical model.

items.method: model proposal with experimental studies (fusion ART neural network)
items.sample: Domains including the Unreal Tournament first-person shooting game and others (truncated)
items.finding: Presents a self-organizing semantic memory model that consolidates knowledge from episodic memory and interacts with procedural memory for more effective decision making. It predates LLM agents but is conceptually related to memory consolidation and interaction.
items.limitations: Not an LLM agent; older neural-network agent setting; abstract truncated.

items.method: method proposal (TiM memory mechanism), evaluation details not in abstract
items.finding: TiM stores historical thoughts in an evolving memory, recalls them before responding and post-thinks to update memory after responding. This is meant to avoid biased, inconsistent reasoning from repeated recall.
items.limitations: Focused on long-term conversation rather than multi-step task success; no results in the abstract; preprint.

items.method: position/conceptual report
items.finding: The report argues that long-term memory is needed for AI self-evolution, letting models evolve at inference time from accumulated interactions and supporting lifelong learning. The abstract states no empirical task-success results.
items.limitations: Conceptual and hypothesis-driven; abstract reports no empirical evaluation; abstract truncated.

items.method: philosophical essay
items.finding: The paper discusses memory, forgetting and reflection in Confucian and virtue epistemology. It does not address LLM agents.
items.limitations: Off-topic philosophical argument; no empirical content.

items.method: proposed system (VIMBank) with experimental comparison against other agents
items.finding: VIMBank is a vector-store long-term memory with dynamic updating and Ebbinghaus forgetting-curve-based forgetting. It reportedly raises task decision success rate by 10-20% over compared agents and cuts reasoning cost by about 23%.
items.limitations: Abstract does not describe benchmarks, baselines, or sample; the venue is lower-tier; gains are self-reported.

items.method: benchmark construction (MemoryAgentBench) and evaluation of memory agents
items.finding: MemoryAgentBench evaluates memory agents on four competencies: accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, and selective forgetting, using incremental multi-turn formats. The abstract is truncated before the results.
items.limitations: Abstract truncated, so results are not visible; preprint.

items.method: conceptual framework
items.finding: The paper proposes a conceptual LLM-supported lifelong learning environment for education, stressing personal world models and reflective practice. It is not about agent memory and task success.
items.limitations: Conceptual and education-focused; no empirical evaluation.

items.method: system description with experimental evaluation
items.finding: ChatEDA is an LLM-based EDA agent that handles task decomposition, script generation and execution, and its fine-tuned AutoMage model outperforms GPT-4. The abstract does not mention long-term memory.
items.limitations: No memory component or ablation described in the abstract; domain-specific.

items.method: system description with benchmarking on course exercises and case studies
items.sample: six university-level course exercises and two case studies
items.finding: El Agente Q uses a hierarchical memory framework within its cognitive architecture and reaches an average task success above 87%. It also supports longer multi-step workflows.
items.limitations: No memory ablation in the abstract, so the memory contribution cannot be isolated; small, domain-specific benchmark.

items.method: survey with taxonomy
items.finding: The survey gives a taxonomy of LLM-agent planning (task decomposition, plan selection, external module, reflection and memory) and discusses open challenges. Memory is treated as one planning-enhancing category.
items.limitations: Planning-focused; the abstract describes no systematic review method and no quantitative memory-effect synthesis.

items.method: survey of agent architectures
items.finding: The survey compares single- and multi-agent architectures and highlights planning, execution and reflection phases that support robust agents. Memory is not explicitly discussed in the abstract.
items.limitations: No stated review method; little memory-specific content in the abstract.

items.method: open-source library/framework description
items.finding: The Agents library supports planning, memory, tool use and multi-agent communication in a modular design for building language agents. The abstract reports no evaluation of memory's effect on task success.
items.limitations: Software description only; no empirical results in the abstract.

items.method: benchmark evaluation of 4 agents on 12 tasks
items.sample: 4 LLM agents, 12 ARA-relevant tasks
items.finding: LM agents could complete only the easiest of the 12 autonomous replication and adaptation tasks, making some progress on harder ones. The abstract says nothing about long-term memory design.
items.limitations: Not about memory; small set of tasks and simple agents; evaluations cannot rule out capabilities of future agents.

items.method: empirical benchmark evaluation (offline and online) on Mind2Web and WebArena
items.sample: 1000+ tasks across 200+ domains
items.finding: Agent Workflow Memory induces reusable workflows from past experience and supplies them to guide the agent. It improves relative success rate by 24.6% on Mind2Web and 51.1% on WebArena and reduces steps on WebArena.
items.limitations: Evaluated only on web navigation benchmarks; the abstract is truncated, so generalization claims are only partly visible.

items.method: model proposal with empirical evaluation on four datasets
items.sample: four trajectory prediction datasets
items.finding: MANTRA uses memory-augmented networks to predict multiple trajectories of other agents, with state-of-the-art results on four datasets. Because the memory is non-parametric, it can keep improving by ingesting new patterns.
items.limitations: Trajectory prediction for pedestrians and vehicles, not LLM agents or multi-step task success.

items.method: conceptual model proposal
items.finding: Proposes a narrative memory module for conscious agents to create, store and recall narrative representations of past experiences. The abstract claims it would improve perception, understanding and decision-making.
items.limitations: No empirical evaluation in the abstract; not LLM-specific; no task success metrics.

items.method: new dataset construction and retrieval model evaluation
items.sample: new dataset of ambiguous and time-based questions built on simulated long-form conversations
items.finding: Standard RAG handles time/event-based and ambiguous queries over long conversations poorly. A new retrieval model combining chain-of-table search and vector-database retrieval is proposed to address this.
items.limitations: Conversational QA rather than multi-step task success; simulated conversations; abstract truncated.

items.method: benchmark evaluation of prompt-injection susceptibility
items.sample: six frontier models on realistic web tasks
items.finding: Agents were susceptible to prompt injection in 25% of tasks on average (13% for GPT-5 to 43% for DeepSeek-R1). Small interface or context changes often doubled attack success.
items.limitations: About security vulnerabilities, not long-term memory.

items.method: method proposal (MemGAS) with empirical evaluation
items.finding: MemGAS uses multi-granularity memory units, GMM-based clustering and association, and an entropy-based router to pick the retrieval granularity. It aims to balance completeness against noise in conversational memory retrieval.
items.limitations: Conversational dialogue memory rather than multi-step task success; abstract truncated, so results are not visible.

items.method: controlled empirical study on ALFWorld with ablated retention policies (two seeds, Wilson CIs)
items.sample: ALFWorld with gpt-5-mini; held-out evaluation of 50 tasks
items.finding: External memory improves over no memory: 47-49 of 50 held-out tasks solved versus 39/50. Bounded retention policies are statistically indistinguishable on clean ALFWorld. Under 75% distractor writes, unbounded memory and FIFO degrade in precision while TraceRetain preserves 97/100 task success.
items.limitations: Single environment and model, two seeds, synthetic noise stress; preprint.

items.method: controlled harness evaluation of memory substrates
items.sample: three backbone models, four benchmark suites, 26 metrics
items.finding: No single memory substrate dominates. Broad retrieval helps long-context factual QA, but excessive retrieval can harm sequential decision-making. Some substrates become costly or brittle at longer horizons.
items.limitations: Preprint; the abstract is truncated, so detailed numbers are not visible.

items.method: benchmark construction with human-crafted multi-session agentic tasks
items.sample: tasks across web navigation, preference-constrained planning, progressive information search and sequential formal reasoning
items.finding: MemoryArena evaluates memory acquisition and use together in multi-session agent-environment loops with interdependent subtasks. The abstract is cut off, but it indicates that agents with near-saturated performance on existing benchmarks do worse here.
items.limitations: Abstract truncated; benchmark paper, so it does not itself compare memory designs; preprint.

items.method: controlled ablation study on ScienceWorld (4 configurations: baseline, +AMM, +SRM, full)
items.sample: ScienceWorld interactive environment
items.finding: The full system (episodic Adaptive Memory Module plus Self-Reflection Module) achieved the best mean score (64.62), success rate (43.17%) and step efficiency (19.33 steps). Self-reflection was the strongest standalone contributor, while episodic memory helped most once the runtime loop was stabilized.
items.limitations: Single benchmark (ScienceWorld); one base agent (SwiftSage); preprint; memory's standalone gain appears modest.

items.method: systematic survey/literature review
items.finding: Surveys memory mechanisms of LLM-based agents: what memory is, why it is needed, how memory modules are designed and evaluated, and application examples. It also analyzes limitations of existing work and future directions.
items.limitations: Survey only, with no new empirical results; the abstract is truncated, so the specific limitations covered are not visible.

items.method: conceptual review and modeling framework
items.finding: Proposes a framework for ethical clinical AI agents, identifying state persistence among the core architectural dimensions. It examines how these features affect bias propagation and error cascades in multi-step workflows.
items.limitations: Conceptual, with no empirical evaluation; healthcare/ethics focus; memory is only one of several dimensions.

items.method: method proposal with experiments on benchmark datasets
items.finding: SAUP propagates step-level uncertainty with situational weights through multistep LLM agent reasoning, improving AUROC by up to 20% over existing uncertainty estimation methods.
items.limitations: Addresses uncertainty estimation and error accumulation across steps, not memory; the abstract gives no benchmark details.

items.method: systematization of knowledge (SoK) from a curated corpus
items.finding: Develops a security framework for autonomous LLM agents in commerce, with 12 cross-layer attack vectors across five threat dimensions. Failures propagate from the reasoning and tooling layers into custody.
items.limitations: Security and commerce focus; the abstract does not address long-term memory design or task success.

items.method: taxonomy-driven survey
items.finding: Presents a modular reference architecture and four-dimensional taxonomy of agentic AI systems, noting design trade-offs, recurring failure modes and evaluation methodologies including operational cost. Memory is not specifically highlighted in the abstract.
items.limitations: Broad survey; memory is not a focus; no systematic review method is stated in the abstract.

items.method: literature survey and taxonomy
items.finding: Proposes a seven-layer trust taxonomy (including memory and retrieval layers) and six secure-coordination design patterns for multi-agent LLM systems. Hallucinations can propagate across agent boundaries.
items.limitations: Focus on security and hallucination in multi-agent systems; memory is only one layer; no empirical evaluation.

items.method: system implementation with reported metrics
items.finding: A multi-agent email response system combining RAG over vector databases and ReAct agents with SQL toolkit reached 91.2% classification accuracy and an 88.4% end-to-end success rate.
items.limitations: Application paper; no memory ablation or comparison; RAG is used for knowledge retrieval rather than long-term agent memory.

items.method: benchmark construction and evaluation
items.sample: 143 multi-session tasks across 19 BIM projects and 4,016 prior sessions
items.finding: Introduces IFCMemoryBench to evaluate long-term memory when agents must combine remembered context from earlier sessions with live IFC queries. The framework decomposes memory performance into ingestion, retrieval and utilization.
items.limitations: Single domain (BIM); the abstract is truncated, so results on specific memory architectures are not visible; preprint.

items.method: paired counterfactual multi-agent rollouts
items.finding: Toxic content compressed into memory summaries can fall below toxicity detection thresholds yet still raise downstream toxicity. Raw transcript reuse drives overt toxicity while compressed memory carries hidden sub-threshold influence (measured by the sub-threshold propagation gap).
items.limitations: Concerns safety/toxicity rather than task success; simulated multi-agent setting; preprint.

items.method: unclear from abstract (system proposal evaluated on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S benchmarks with GPT-4.1-mini and Qwen3-8B; abstract truncated)
items.finding: LeanMem is a lightweight long-term memory framework that filters low-value content and stores it as profile, event, or record memory. It selectively updates only evolving event memories and adapts memory type and retrieval budget to each query, aiming to cut token use without losing fine-grained evidence. Quantitative results are cut off in the abstract.
items.limitations: Abstract is truncated, so results are not visible. The benchmarks are conversational memory (LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S) rather than multi-step task success. It is a preprint with no citations.

items.method: conceptual/theoretical article
items.finding: The paper argues that dynamic capabilities in firms require blending analytic and intuitive cognitive and emotional processes, drawing on social cognitive neuroscience. It does not address LLM agents.
items.limitations: Off-topic: strategic management; 'reflexion/reflection' is unrelated to LLM agent memory.

items.method: narrative review
items.finding: Reviews evidence on the relation between attention and memory across working memory, long-term memory, development and neuropsychology, organized by an embedded-processes view.
items.limitations: Human cognitive psychology; no LLM agents or task success measures.

items.method: laboratory conditioning experiments
items.sample: harnessed honeybees (n not stated in abstract)
items.finding: Honeybees learn side-specific associative mechanosensory conditioning of the proboscis extension reflex, with memory still present 24 h later and an optimal interstimulus interval around 4 s.
items.limitations: Off-topic: insect reflex conditioning; unrelated to LLM agents.

items.method: unclear from abstract
items.finding: The abstract contains only a licensing statement and no substantive content. The title suggests a history/memory framework for history education, unrelated to LLM agents.
items.limitations: No usable abstract; off-topic.

items.method: laboratory conditioning experiments
items.sample: harnessed honeybees (n not stated in abstract)
items.finding: Intact harnessed bees can learn visual discrimination via sting extension reflex conditioning with shock punishment, and antennae ablation impaired rather than helped learning.
items.limitations: Off-topic: insect learning; unrelated to LLM agents.

items.method: neurophysiological recordings in anesthetized animals
items.sample: 4 infant macaques
items.finding: NOT-DTN neurons in infant macaques are direction selective shortly after birth but have lower selectivity, truncated velocity tuning and weaker V1 input than adults.
items.limitations: Off-topic: primate visual neuroscience; very small sample.

items.method: narrative historical review and theory proposal
items.finding: Proposes a theory of autonomic socioemotional reflexes in mother-infant co-regulation after a narrative history of nervous system theories.
items.limitations: Off-topic theoretical paper on developmental psychology; no empirical test in the abstract.

items.method: modeling/methods comparison of pupil size equations
items.finding: Presents and compares models to calculate pupil size from luminance, age and other parameters so the pupillary light reflex can be decoupled from other influences.
items.limitations: Off-topic: pupillometry; memory is mentioned only as a possible pupil influence.

items.method: method proposal with benchmark experiments
items.sample: HotpotQA and ALFWorld with various backbone LLMs
items.finding: KnowAgent uses an action knowledge base and self-learning to constrain planning paths, achieving comparable or superior performance to baselines and reducing planning hallucination.
items.limitations: Knowledge base is explicit action knowledge rather than long-term experiential memory; abstract gives no numeric results or memory ablation.

items.method: method proposal with benchmark evaluation
items.sample: interactive instruction-following benchmark, seen and unseen environments
items.finding: CAPEAM combines context-aware planning with environment-aware memory of object states and locations, reaching state-of-the-art results with up to +10.70% gain in unseen environments.
items.limitations: Embodied household agent rather than a pure LLM agent; memory is task-episode environment state; abstract does not isolate the memory ablation.

items.method: single-system production deployment case study (90 days), no stated baseline beyond manual comparison
items.sample: One IT infrastructure management deployment (Proxmox, Kubernetes, networking, security) over 90 days
items.finding: Mind-Tool, which combines a persistent memory layer, a desired-state goal model and a reasoning engine, reported a 94% task success rate, 68% workflow automation and 62% time reduction versus manual approaches. The authors argue that domain memory design matters more than model intelligence.
items.limitations: Single deployment with no memory ablation, so the effect of memory cannot be isolated. The comparison is against manual work, not other agents. Self-reported results from the system's own authors, and the claim that it validates Anthropic's work is asserted, not tested.

items.method: narrative/systematic review with a mathematical formalization of CBR; no clear review protocol stated
items.finding: The paper reviews how Case-Based Reasoning (case retrieval, adaptation, learning) can be integrated into LLM agents to supply experience-based memory. It compares CBR-enhanced agents with Chain-of-Thought and standard RAG and discusses the role of self-reflection and other cognitive dimensions.
items.limitations: Abstract gives no review protocol, number of studies or quantitative success-rate results. Conceptual and theoretical focus, and the abstract is truncated.
